digital-culture.title: Behind the rise of the chief productivity officer and what it means for companies and employees
digital-culture.excerpt: Some employers are replacing HR directors with chief productivity officers to better align people, tech and business outcomes.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Some companies are ditching traditional HR director roles and replacing them with chief productivity officers who focus on connecting people, technology, and business results. This matters because it signals a fundamental shift in how organizations think about work itself: less about compliance and benefits, more about output and efficiency. Honestly, this could go either way. Smart CPOs will recognize that real productivity comes from trusting people and fixing broken processes. Bad ones will just become surveillance enthusiasts with fancier job titles.
